definitions.name: Pro-rata
definitions.definition: Each year's spending comes from every accessible account in proportion to its balance (Tax Deferred and Roth gains only from 59½).

definitions.name: Tax-optimized (gains first)
definitions.definition: The app's order. Brokerage while its gains are taxed at 0%, then Tax Deferred up to the start of the 22% bracket (or less, to keep those gains at 0%), then more Brokerage at 15/20%, then more Tax Deferred, then Roth. Any 0% capital gains room left over is harvested.

definitions.name: Tax Deferred to 22% line first (previous)
definitions.definition: The earlier tax-optimized order: Tax Deferred up to the start of the 22% bracket, then Brokerage, then more Tax Deferred, then Roth.

definitions.name: Brokerage > Tax Deferred > Roth
definitions.definition: The conventional rule of thumb: Brokerage until it's empty, then Tax Deferred, then Roth.

definitions.name: Tax Deferred > Brokerage > Roth
definitions.definition: Drain Tax Deferred first: Tax Deferred until it's empty, then Brokerage, then Roth.

definitions.name: Greedy lowest marginal tax
definitions.definition: Each chunk of spending ($1,000, or 1/25 of the year's need if larger) comes from whichever of Tax Deferred and Brokerage adds the least tax this year; Roth last.

definitions.name: Tax-optimized, no 0% harvesting
definitions.definition: W2 without the 0% capital gains harvesting, to isolate what harvesting adds.

definitions.name: To 22% line, protecting 0% gains (app)
definitions.definition: The app's policy. Up to the start of the 22% bracket, or lower when more ordinary income would push the gains already realized this year out of the 0% capital gains band.

definitions.name: To 22% line, ignoring 0% gains
definitions.definition: Up to the start of the 22% bracket, even if that moves this year's 0% gains to 15%.

definitions.name: To top of 22% bracket
definitions.definition: Up to the top of the 22% bracket.

definitions.name: To top of 24% bracket
definitions.definition: Up to the top of the 24% bracket.
